data.question: In this floor plan, near the SW (bottom-left) corner of the building, is there a door opening in the WEST (left) exterior wall or in the SOUTH (bottom) exterior wall of the room at bottom-left? Describe exactly which wall the door arc/swing symbol is drawn in, near the dimensions '540, 900, 2000' along the bottom wall.

response.result:
Based on my examination of the floor plan, I can now clearly identify the door location.

Looking at the bottom-left (SW corner) area of the building where the dimensions "540, 900, 2000" are marked along the bottom wall:

**The door opening is drawn in the SOUTH (bottom) exterior wall.**

The door arc (cyan curved line) is clearly visible in the original image at approximately **original pixel coordinates around x=280-380, y=400-480**. The arc's curved swing symbol opens upward into the room from the SOUTH exterior wall (the bottom horizontal wall of the building), not from the WEST wall.

The arc pattern shows the door hinge positioned on the south exterior boundary, with the door swinging into the interior room above it. This is the classic architectural representation of a south-facing exterior door opening northward into the room's interior space.

source_geometry_self_consistency.scope: source geometry, contacts and explicit opening hosts

agent_assumptions: Plan top edge = North, bottom edge = South, left = West, right = East (no compass mark provided; confirmed by matching South elevation entrance door position x=[3.44,4.64] to plan bottom-row door, and North elevation 3-window pattern to plan top-row offices).
Wall thickness ~0.24m per plan annotations; modeled as zero-thickness representative planes at wall centerlines (cells abut at shared coordinate, no interior wall voids added).
Ground floor (F1) height 3.0m, first floor (F2) height 3.6m, total 6.6m, per East/West elevation vertical dimension breakdown (3600+3000 blocks split by mid slab).
Window sill/head heights: F1 windows z=[1.0,2.6]; F2 windows z=[4.0,5.8] (absolute), read from elevation vertical dimension chains (1000 sill/1600 or 1800 height/remainder to ceiling).

Door heights: 2.1m for interior doors; 2.4m for the two main exterior glazed doors (South main entrance, West corridor entrance) per elevation door proportions; 2.1m for the newly added secondary south exterior door (single-leaf, plainer glyph than the double-glazed main entrance) per South_view.png proportions.

East facade has a window (not door) into the corridor on both floors; West facade has a matching-position door into the corridor on F1 and a window in the same position on F2, confirmed by comparing East_view.png and West_view.png door/window glyphs.

Each of the 3 north and 3 south F1 rooms, and each F2 room (2 conference + 4 offices), has exactly one door to the central corridor, per arc marks in 1f_view.png/2f_view.png; F1's two arcs flanking each internal partition belong to the two different adjacent rooms, not a single double door.

Interior room-to-corridor door exact widths/positions along the shared wall are approximated (~0.75-1m, placed near the partition/jamb marks visible in the drawing); precise jamb offsets for F2 office doors were not individually pixel-verified (flagged uncertain in review).

F1_R1S has TWO exterior south doors: the main double-glazed entrance D_main at x=[3.44,4.64], and a second, previously unmodeled single-leaf exterior door D_R1S_ext2 at x=[0.54,1.44] near the SW corner, confirmed both by a wall-gap+arc in 1f_view.png (dims 540/900 from corner) and by a distinct single-leaf door glyph in South_view.png left of the ground-floor windows.
unresolved: Exact interior door widths/positions for F2 office-to-corridor doors (D_Off1_C..D_Off4_C) are approximated/centered rather than pixel-verified against the small 360/660mm jamb dimensions on 2f_view.png.
Door swing direction/leaf count (single vs double) not modeled, only presence and connectivity.
Room role labels (office/lounge/meeting) are descriptive, based on furniture drawn, not authoritative naming from the source drawings.

D_R1S_ext2 height (2.1m) is an assumption based on visual proportion in South_view.png relative to the main entrance and floor height dimension chain (1500/900/600=3000mm); not independently dimensioned in the source.
